rows.title: What’s Working: Techstars teams with startup community to bring back Boulder accelerator
rows.standfirst: The company also had its latest Demo Day for startups with new tech for workforce development.

rows.title: Electric gridlock: Can the growing West’s infrastructure evolve fast enough to keep the lights on?
rows.standfirst: A booming population, data centers, cryptocurrency mines, the electrification of manufacturing are all boosting electricity demand. What’s Colorado’s plan?

rows.title: Finding a fit: Social skills are key for college grads entering a challenging job market
rows.standfirst: Colorado job openings are flat, as tech economy softens and federal policy impacts job prospects. Social capital nonprofits help a diverse workforce find employment.

rows.title: Colorado outdoor businesses are struggling under tariff uncertainty
rows.standfirst: At a Denver U.S. Senate committee hearing on small business last week, three Colorado outdoor entrepreneurs told Sen. John Hickenlooper their businesses were threatened by the Trump trade war

rows.title: Why two regional grid operators are racing to pool the power of Western states like Colorado
rows.standfirst: Colorado power companies have until 2030 to join wholesale markets that can help balance demand for electricity and also develop creative financing strategies for transmission projects

rows.title: Colorado must redo its affordable broadband plan to adhere to new federal rules
rows.standfirst: The state was nearly done finalizing grants. It now must restart the process after the federal BEAD program was criticized for high costs of building fiber instead of cheaper options. A beneficiary is Starlink, which was founded by Elon Musk.

rows.title: Colorado towns take new approach to force oil and gas company to plug old wells
rows.standfirst: Fast-growing communities in Weld County are using revised rules to petition K.P. Kauffman to plug and abandon wells they see as threats to the safety of homes

rows.title: As A Special Place shutters, a new operator plans to reopen in outraged Grand Junction neighborhood
rows.standfirst: The nonprofit that tested a new housing law with supportive housing for people with criminal and mental health issues was open for less than six months, but another health care provider is swooping in.

rows.title: Colorado joins California, other states suing to preserve electric vehicle mandates after Trump cancels them
rows.standfirst: Rules to sell only EVs in the 2030s are at risk in major dustup over state vs. federal rights

rows.title: What’s Working: How Enstrom Candies almost left downtown Grand Junction
rows.standfirst: The candy maker is expanding in town, next to land it sold to the city for affordable housing. Plus: Another Colorado grocery strike?

rows.title: Colorado workers at 4 Safeway stores and a Denver distribution center go on strike
rows.standfirst: Grocery workers involved in the strike work at stores in Estes Park, Fountain and Pueblo. More expected to join this week. The Albertsons-owned chain has 105 stores in the state.

rows.title: As Colorado ages, seniors are colliding with the housing crisis
rows.standfirst: Most older residents want to age in place. But experts say Colorado’s housing stock wasn’t built with their needs in mind.

rows.title: A pair of CU hockey buds are brewing up business with recycled coffee waste
rows.standfirst: The owners of Blazin’ Joe fire logs are pushing recycling innovation in Colorado, which has lagged behind other states in sustainable waste systems.

rows.title: Beloved grocery store serving secluded Colorado town of 500 people looks for ways to buy local
rows.standfirst: The Walsh Community Grocery Store was resurrected in 2007 with the help of its residents. Seventeen years later, its manager is looking for creative ways to stock the shelves.

rows.title: Safeway workers in more parts of Colorado hit the picket lines amid union’s strike
rows.standfirst: Stores in Littleton and Castle Rock joined the strike on Monday. Grocery workers in other states also appear poised to strike at stores owned by Kroger and Albertsons

rows.title: What the Colorado legislature did — and didn’t — do this year to address the housing crisis
rows.standfirst: Lawmakers cracked down on “junk fees” in rental agreements, created new tools to combat negligent landlords and built on efforts to increase density. But other proposals fell short.

rows.title: Rocky Ford was a finalist for an environmental justice grant. Then Trump stepped in.
rows.standfirst: “It didn’t just cancel a funding stream. It sent a message that rural communities like Rocky Ford … don’t matter,” said Mayor Duane Gurulé.

rows.title: A Salida rancher asks if it’s time to rethink permanent conservation easements. “Perpetuity is not working.”
rows.standfirst: The Hutchinson Ranch — the oldest family-owned cattle operation in the Upper Arkansas River Valley — wanted a concert to generate critical revenue. The Colorado Cattlemen’s Agricultural Land Trust said no.

rows.title: Xcel using eminent domain to clear a route for its Power Pathway transmission line in Elbert County
rows.standfirst: Colorado’s largest utility says acquiring right of way for the 550-mile loop to bring power from wind and solar on the Eastern Plains has gone smoothly — but for 48 miles in Elbert County

rows.title: Young homebuyers face high hurdles to ownership. These programs may help.
rows.standfirst: From time-tested budgeting methods to creative financing products, there are several ways young homebuyers can still purchase their first home

rows.title: GOP plan to sell more than 3,200 square miles of federal lands is found to violate Senate rules
rows.standfirst: A plan to sell more than 3,200 square miles of federal lands has been ruled out of Republicans’ big tax and spending cut bill after the Senate parliamentarian determined the proposal by Senate Energy Chairman Mike Lee would violate the chamber’s rules.

rows.title: Colorado losing a third major clean energy project as subsidy cuts, tariffs roil markets
rows.standfirst: Amprius Technologies says it will not move forward on a $190 million battery plant in Brighton touted by Gov. Polis and Adams County

rows.title: Colorado’s post-COVID tech startup scene looks a lot like it did 20 years ago
rows.standfirst: The meetups, the money, the momentum are back as the tech scene in Boulder, Denver welcomes a revival

rows.title: Elbert County says no to Xcel Energy’s Power Pathway permit request
rows.standfirst: Commissioners are irked the state’s largest utility started suing residents for eminent domain before it had permits for a crucial route through their rural county

rows.title: “Negligent” K.P. Kauffman won’t be forced by regulators to plug 39 Weld County wells
rows.standfirst: The embattled oil and gas operator does have to plug and clean up three wells within the next 12 months, but ECMC finds others aren’t a threat to public safety

rows.title: Colorado regulators move to hold Chevron accountable for massive Weld County well blow out
rows.standfirst: 7-square miles around Galeton has been divided into 300 parcels, each with its own cleanup plan, after spill ECMC called “extremely rare”

rows.title: Pueblo steel mill sold to US private equity company Atlas Holdings
rows.standfirst: $500 million deal for Evraz North America is expected to close later this year. State economic development officials are optimistic about the transaction.

rows.title: Selling off Colorado: Tech bros and conservatives have grand plans for federal lands
rows.standfirst: But does anybody who lives here actually like the idea of trading U.S. forests for apartments, or high-desert mesas for “freedom cities”?

rows.title: Latest US budget bill even worse for Colorado clean energy despite pushback, advocates say
rows.standfirst: Senate added a new 50% tax on utilities building solar or wind with foreign parts, while also killing all personal and large-scale clean subsidies
